ratings_why.fun: Every turn asks how to move one number: borrow to arm Skimmers, sell into Uncle Jack, or let Mr Magpie hold the bill, and the builds really pull against each other.
ratings_why.distinct: Debt as a live fight resource that kills pay down is unlike today's tribes, though many payoffs end as plain +X/+X per trigger.

verdict_why: Nothing is broken or unreadable now; further passes would mostly reshuffle the same strong web.

points.text: Tower Raven's Start of Combat Borrow lands before or after The Black Feather and Hooded Crow Heavy read Debt depending on slot order. Say so in the rulings: it is a lovely hidden placement puzzle.
Grandmother Corbie only counts the Ledger and asks nothing of you. A twist, like spending Ledger or rewarding a turn with several repayments, would make the capstone a decision.
Penny Jackdaw is a plain Borrow. A small hook, such as Skim 1 or a Repaid trigger, would let the Tier 1 tempo body feed the count or lump line too.
Moving Mr Magpie forward to call the bill is the best decision in the tribe; a second card that cares which row it sits in would deepen it.

standouts.why: Mr Magpie turns a free board move into choosing when the bill lands, and it fights the Skim build.
Uncle Jack makes every sale, from any tribe, a repayment, so Birds, Oozes and Created junk all become fuel.
Thought and Memory multiplies events, not stats, so it rewards whichever line you built and makes golden Skim's count-to-lump shift matter.

weakest.why: Penny Jackdaw is gold now, broke next turn, with no other hook.
Grandmother Corbie is a passive Ledger counter with no choice in it.
Silas Glint is plain gold per Skim and adds little to the web beyond Seven and Belfry Mob.

flags.note: Tower Raven with enough Skimmers is 3 free gold every fight; Debt caps it, but worth the owner's eye.
Seven with The Belfry Mob and Tower Raven can make five to seven permanent tribe-wide +1/+1 a fight.
Arne with Thought and Memory on a Mr Magpie bill is the noted high roll, about 10 bodies at once.
